calls.head: Strength against strength
calls.body: The Ducks are one of the league’s best for shot volume, and the Golden Knights are one of the league’s best at keeping shots away. We’ll side with the Ducks.
calls.call: The Ducks take more than the league-average 56.7 shot attempts per 60 at 5-on-5 against the Golden Knights.
calls.nums: Anaheim 4th for shot volume (62.9 shot attempts per 60 at 5-on-5) · Vegas 5th for keeping shots away
calls.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 0 and 1 games this season
calls.happened: On 5-on-5 shot attempts, Anaheim had 55.9 per 60. The league average is 56.7 per 60, and they came in at 62.9 per 60.

calls.head: The Ducks’ goalie is in for some dangerous shots
calls.body: The Golden Knights make their shots count, and the Ducks are one of the league’s worst at preventing dangerous shots. Expect the Golden Knights to get some real chances.
calls.call: The Golden Knights’ average shot has at least their usual 6.5% chance of going in.
calls.nums: Vegas 9th for shot quality (a 6.5% chance of scoring on the average shot) · Anaheim 28th for preventing dangerous shots
calls.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 1 and 0 games this season
calls.happened: Vegas’s average shot had a 6.2% chance of going in, against their usual 6.5%.

VGK.head: We had this close to even (60% for Vegas), and it went Anaheim’s way.

ANA.head: We had this close to even (40% for Anaheim), and Anaheim came through.

surprises.head: Anaheim got the good looks
surprises.body: Anaheim’s shots at 5-on-5 were more dangerous than usual: an 8.3% chance of scoring on the average shot, against their usual 6.2% (league average 6.3%). A team strays this far about once every 15 games.

surprises.head: Anaheim leaned on their bottom six
surprises.body: Anaheim’s bottom-six forwards played 45% of the forwards’ 5-on-5 time, against their usual 41% and a league average of 42%. A team strays this far about once every 15 games.

story.head: The Ducks beat the Golden Knights
paras: Beckett Sennecke opened the scoring late in the first. Four different Ducks scored. Leo Carlsson scored the winner midway through the second.
The Golden Knights had the better of the play. Replay the chances a hundred times and the Golden Knights win about six in ten.

items.text: None of the preview’s two calls held.
